verdict.rationale: Working Copy's manual documents both halves of the story: an Amend toggle in the commit dialog for changing the latest commit, and a swipe-to-Undo for unpushed commits that leaves their changes in the working directory. Hunk-level staging then lets you recommit those changes as separate, split commits, and Edit Message, Squash and Delete Commit extend history editing. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the amend/undo/split workflow.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can amend the latest commit or undo unpushed commits to fix or split them

citations.quote: To make changes to the latest commit enable Amend at the top of the commit dialog.
For commits not yet pushed to a remote, swipe left to Undo them. The commit's changes remain in your working directory as modified files
you can stage/unstage individual hunks by long-tapping and swiping making it possible to commit some changes in a file but leave others uncommitted.
Long tapping commits you can Delete Commit to rewrite the branch without the work contributed by this single commit, Edit Message to change a commit message... or Squash a commit with its child.
